items.title: Vi Redd interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 13, 1999
items.q: I’d play one night and Hampton Hawes would have a band there the other night.

ctx.x: During World War II, when a lot of the fellows were in the service, did that make a difference for the opportunities for women?

Well see I was still in school then. I didn’t really start until ’48, that’s when I got out of high school. But see I wasn’t playing then. My father wouldn’t let me come in the clubs, that was taboo. You know at that age. I got started really like in the early 50s, and the late — oh ’48, ’49 is when I got my little band together and I started playing all these sorority events and things like that. Sororities, fraternity dances, we used to play over at the place call the Alpha Bowling Club. It’s a church now. And…
When was your first opportunity to record?
